HL OOP Scenario 01

Darwin's Museum

From Theropods to Birds: Deep Inheritance & Polymorphism

The Scenario

Darwin returns from an expedition with fossils and living specimens. The museum is opening a new exhibit called "From Theropods to Birds". A tour guide introduces visitors to each exhibit. Your task is to implement the specimen classes so the exhibit tour can run — demonstrating the evolutionary connection between fearsome dinosaurs and modern birds.

Learning Objectives

1
Build a multi-level inheritance chain (Species → Dinosaur → Theropod → TRex)
2
Create parallel inheritance branches (Species → Bird → Chicken)
3
Demonstrate polymorphism by calling the same method on different object types
4
Use @property decorator for encapsulation (read-only specimen IDs)

Class Hierarchy

Method Specifications

Each method below must be implemented. This is what each method should do — how you implement it is up to you.

Species (base class)

Method Returns Expected Behavior
__init__(specimen_id) None Store the specimen_id as a private attribute. Initialize all attributes shown in the UML with sensible defaults.
specimen_id (property) str Return the private specimen ID. This must be read-only — use Python's @property decorator.
describe() str Return a description of the species using species_name and common_name.
sound() str Return text describing the sound this species makes (e.g., "ROAR", "BAWK", "HONK").
move() str Return text describing how this species moves (walking, flying, swimming, etc.).

Dinosaur (inherits from Species)

Method Returns Expected Behavior
__init__(specimen_id) None Call super().__init__() first, then set dinosaur-specific attributes (clade, tail_length_m, has_feathers).
get_skeletal_note() str Return a string describing skeletal features using clade and tail_length_m.

Theropod (inherits from Dinosaur)

Method Returns Expected Behavior
hunt() str Return text describing how this theropod hunts, mentioning its hunting_style attribute.
get_trait_evolution() str Return a summary of evolved traits using hand_claws and stance.

TRex (inherits from Theropod)

Method Returns Expected Behavior
intimidate() str Return text describing an intimidation display, mentioning the T-Rex's bite force.
get_museum_fact() str Return an interesting museum-worthy fact about T-Rex (e.g., about its tiny arms or massive bite).

Velociraptor (inherits from Theropod)

Method Returns Expected Behavior
pack_hunt() str Return text describing coordinated pack hunting, mentioning pack_size.
leap_attack() str Return text describing the signature leaping attack with its claw_length_cm sickle claw.

Bird (inherits from Species)

Method Returns Expected Behavior
lay_eggs() str Return text about egg-laying behavior.

Chicken (inherits from Bird)

Method Returns Expected Behavior
forage() str Return text describing foraging behavior (scratching ground for food).

Penguin (inherits from Bird)

Method Returns Expected Behavior
swim() str Return text describing swimming ability, mentioning swim_speed_kmh.
huddle() str Return text describing the huddling behavior for warmth, mentioning colony_size.
💡 Overriding: Subclasses should override inherited methods like sound() and move() to return behavior specific to that species. A T-Rex's sound() should return a roar, while a Chicken's should return a cluck.

Your Task

What You Need to Build

  1. Study the UML diagram above — it contains all the attributes and methods you need
  2. Build the Species base class first: this is the foundation everything inherits from
  3. Follow the Dinosaur branch down: Dinosaur → Theropod → (TRex | Velociraptor)
  4. Follow the Bird branch down: Bird → (Chicken | Penguin)
  5. In main.py, create one instance of each class and add them to a single list
  6. Loop through your list and call sound(), move(), and describe() on each — this is polymorphism
💡 The Big Idea: A TRex and a Chicken both inherit from Species, so they both have a sound() method. But when you call it, you get a roar vs a cluck. Same method name, different behavior — that's polymorphism. Your museum tour should demonstrate this.

Success Criteria

✓
All 8 classes match the UML hierarchy exactly
✓
Each subclass correctly calls super().__init__()
✓
Looping through a mixed list shows different outputs for the same method call
✓
specimen_id uses @property and cannot be changed after creation
